prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t honestly name one single “best” lawyer for every car-wreck case — the right attorney depends on your injuries, insurance issues, budget, and whether you need a trial lawyer or a settlement-focused negotiator. I can, however, help you find the best lawyer for your situation. A quick way to proceed: tell me your ZIP code and a few facts about the crash (severity of injuries, fault disputed, insurance limits, any deadline concerns) and I’ll give a short, tailored shortlist and what to ask them.

Meanwhile, here’s how to choose a top personal injury lawyer in Houston and what to do right now:

What to look for in a Houston car-wreck lawyer
- Relevant experience: frequent handling of car-accident cases and experience with cases like yours (catastrophic injury, amputation, brain injury, wrongful death, or soft-tissue/whiplash).
- Trial experience: a lawyer who will try the case if the insurer won’t offer fair value.
- Track record: documented verdicts/large settlements in similar cases (ask for examples).
- Communication and availability: clear point of contact and timely updates.
- Fee structure: most take cases on contingency (commonly 33–40% if the case settles, possibly higher if it goes to suit), plus who pays case expenses.
- Medical management: ability to coordinate care, handle medical liens, and work with treating providers.
- Local reputation: peer reviews, client reviews, memberships (e.g., local trial lawyer associations).
- Clean disciplinary record: check the State Bar of Texas for complaints or sanctions.

How to verify and where to look
- State Bar of Texas website — confirm license and disciplinary record.
- Court records — search Harris County civil filings for verdicts/appeals.
- Third-party ratings/reviews — Martindale-Hubbell, Google, Avvo, Yelp (use reviews cautiously).
- Referrals from doctors or other lawyers.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the outcomes?
- Will you personally handle my case or a junior attorney/associate?
- What is your contingency fee and how are costs handled?
- Do you have trial experience in Harris County courts?
- How long will this likely take, and what is a realistic settlement range?
- Can you give references from recent clients?

Immediate steps after a wreck (if you haven’t already)
- Seek and follow medical care — your health and medical records are critical.
- Report the crash to police and get the report number.
- Preserve evidence: photos, videos, witness names/contacts.
- Do not give recorded statements to the insurer without talking to a lawyer.
- Document lost wages and expenses.
- Note Texas deadlines: personal injury and wrongful-death suits generally must be filed within two years from the date of the crash (ask a lawyer immediately if you’re near that limit).

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and a brief case summary and I’ll suggest 3–5 Houston lawyers or firms that are a good fit and give suggested first-call questions.
